components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The Signal Amber action — one per view, weight 600, harbor-dark text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--theme-accent, #ffac02); color: var(--theme-bg, #041c1c); padding: 8px 16px; border: none; border-radius: 0.5rem; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.875rem; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 150ms ease, transform 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--theme-focus, #ffac02); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Quiet secondary action; fills with the panel tone on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--theme-text, #ffe6cb); padding: 8px 16px; border: 1px solid var(--theme-border, rgba(255,230,203,0.2)); border-radius: 0.5rem; font-weight: 500; font-size: 0.875rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease, border-color 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--theme-panel, #06282a); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--theme-focus, #ffac02); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard field: input-tone fill, hairline border, amber focus ring.
components.css: .ds-input { background: var(--theme-input, #06282a); color: var(--theme-text, #ffe6cb); border: 1px solid var(--theme-border, rgba(255,230,203,0.2)); border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; width: 240px; transition: border-color 150ms ease; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--composer-placeholder, rgba(255,230,203,0.45)); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--theme-focus, #ffac02); outline-offset: 1px; border-color: var(--theme-focus, #ffac02); }

components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; background: var(--theme-sidebar, #06282a); padding: 8px; border-radius: 0.75rem; width: 200px; } .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; color: var(--theme-muted, rgba(255,230,203,0.6)); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; padding: 8px 10px; border-radius: 0.5rem; transition: background 150ms ease, color 150ms ease; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--theme-card, #082f31); color: var(--theme-text, #ffe6cb); } .ds-nav-item--active { background: var(--theme-accent-subtle, rgba(255,172,2,0.12)); color: var(--theme-accent, #ffac02); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--theme-focus, #ffac02); outline-offset: 1px; }

narrative.overview: Hermes Workspace is not an admin panel you visit; it is a basecamp you and your agents inhabit. The reference energy is Discord, not Jira: warm chat surfaces you can live in for hours, a sidebar with presence and life, an agent that reads as a character rather than a form field. The chrome is technical and confident — deep harbor-night surfaces, instruments that glow amber when they matter — but never cold. The system's single most important structural fact is the theme contract: every color flows through the semantic --theme-* layer, implemented by fourteen first-class themes; the default and canonical palette is Nous (harbor-night teal, lantern cream, signal amber), and every rule must survive a theme swap.
keyCharacteristics: Inhabited, not administered: presence, avatars, live activity everywhere it's honest.
Deep tonal surfaces with one amber voice; personality lives in the theme layer.
Dense enough for an ops console, warm enough for an all-day chat home.
Alive but disciplined: fast 150–200ms feedback, uniform component vocabulary.

rules.name: The Theme Contract Rule
rules.body: No component ever hardcodes a color. Every fill, border, and text color flows through a --theme-* variable. A feature is not done until it looks intentional in all fourteen themes, both modes.

rules.name: The One Lantern Rule
rules.body: Signal Amber (and each theme's accent counterpart) covers at most ~10% of any screen: actions, current selection, live indicators. Amber used decoratively is a bug.

rules.name: The No Foreign Gray Rule
rules.body: Muted text and borders are transparencies of Lantern Cream over teal, never a neutral gray dropped onto the palette.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears exactly where output belongs to the system (code, terminal, logs, IDs) — never as decoration on human-facing labels or buttons.

rules.name: The Fixed Scale Rule
rules.body: Type sizes are fixed rem steps (scale ≈1.2); nothing fluid, nothing clamped. This is product UI viewed at consistent DPI.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: If a layer boundary needs expressing, reach for the next surface tone and a hairline border before reaching for a shadow. Shadows respond to state (hover, floating, modal); they do not decorate rest.

dos: Do route every color through the --theme-* contract and test new UI in at least Nous, one light theme, and one high-character theme (Matrix/Dracula) before calling it done.
Do keep body-text contrast ≥4.5:1 in every theme (WCAG 2.1 AA) — including placeholders and muted text on tinted surfaces.
Do give every interactive element the full state set: default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, error.
Do keep transitions 150–250ms with ease-out curves, and provide prefers-reduced-motion alternatives for anything that moves.
Do show the system's liveness honestly — streaming tokens, worker status, presence — that's the product's soul.
donts: Don't import the glossy SaaS landing kit: no gradient text, no glassmorphism-as-decoration, no hero-metric blocks.
Don't drift toward Jira-like enterprise heaviness: stacked forms, endless toolbars, configuration mazes.
Don't let any screen read as a bare chat wrapper — one lonely chat column indistinguishable from a ChatGPT clone.
Don't hardcode a hex in a component; that's a theme-contract violation even when it matches Nous.
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left > 1px as accent), foreign grays, or decorative motion that conveys no state.
Don't put JetBrains Mono on buttons, labels, or headings — the machine voice is for machine output.
